question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping maintains firm control over the Chinese Communist Party through loyalist appointments, repeated anti-corruption purges in the military and Central Committee, and the absence of any designated successor or organized internal challenge. Recent leadership meetings and personnel reshuffles through mid-2026 have further consolidated his authority rather than signaling transition, with the 21st Party Congress still months away and widely expected to affirm continuity into a fourth term. Traders assign 95% probability to "No" because formal removal mechanisms are absent, elite cohesion appears intact under surveillance and patronage systems, and no verifiable developments indicate imminent departure before the market's December 2026 close. Unlikely but plausible shifts could stem from an acute health crisis, a major policy reversal sparking elite discontent, or an unforeseen external shock disrupting the current power equilibrium.

eventMetadata.context_description: The wide-open 2028 Democratic presidential nomination features no dominant contender, with trader consensus pricing Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez highest at 20.6% followed closely by Jon Ossoff and Gavin Newsom in the mid-teens. This fragmentation stems from the absence of formal announcements nearly two years before primaries, combined with a newly approved DNC calendar that elevates South Carolina, Nevada, and other early states where Black, Latino, and union voters hold influence. Potential candidates span progressive, moderate, and gubernatorial ranks—including Kamala Harris, Pete Buttigieg, Josh Shapiro, and Mark Kelly—each drawing support from distinct party factions and regional bases. Recent polling and market shifts show Newsom's earlier lead eroding as younger or Senate-based figures gain visibility through media and events. The even spread reflects uncertainty over electability factors such as swing-state appeal and primary dynamics, with separation likely hinging on 2027 positioning, fundraising, and state-level developments.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the named individual wins and accepts the 2028 nomination of the Democratic Party for U.S. president. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of official Democratic Party sources.

Any replacement of the democratic nominee before election day will not change the resolution of the market.

eventMetadata.context_description: The wide-open 2028 Democratic presidential nomination features no dominant contender, with trader consensus pricing Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez highest at 20.6% followed closely by Jon Ossoff and Gavin Newsom in the mid-teens. This fragmentation stems from the absence of formal announcements nearly two years before primaries, combined with a newly approved DNC calendar that elevates South Carolina, Nevada, and other early states where Black, Latino, and union voters hold influence. Potential candidates span progressive, moderate, and gubernatorial ranks—including Kamala Harris, Pete Buttigieg, Josh Shapiro, and Mark Kelly—each drawing support from distinct party factions and regional bases. Recent polling and market shifts show Newsom's earlier lead eroding as younger or Senate-based figures gain visibility through media and events. The even spread reflects uncertainty over electability factors such as swing-state appeal and primary dynamics, with separation likely hinging on 2027 positioning, fundraising, and state-level developments.
